item.title: Wild–urban gradient leads to ecological stratification in Singapore’s long-tailed macaques
item.content:encoded:
Nature Cities, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00535-8

This study assessed the diet, gut bacteria and habitat preferences of long-tailed macaques in Singapore across a gradient of urbanization. Animal dietary diversity and gut bacterial diversity both declined with urbanization, while dietary plant diversity varied with urbanization according to ecological category. The macaque population exhibits eight female-line groups associated with specific habitats ranging in degree of urbanicity.

item.title: Maternal mental health liveability shaped by composite residential environmental profiles
item.content:encoded:
Nature Cities, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00534-9

In a cohort of 216,000+ pregnant women across China, air pollution and heat were linked to higher risks of prenatal mental distress, while nearby green space was protective. Urban greening could support maternal mental health and healthier cities.
item.dc:title: Maternal mental health liveability shaped by composite residential environmental profiles
